title: Udio Pricing 2026: Plans, Credits and Free Tier
summary: Udio pricing includes free and paid tiers with different credit limits. See which plan matches your music generation needs.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


The questions left over are mostly about what the free tier and a paid plan cover, so each answer below is marked by whether Udio's own pages settle it. Where I couldn't confirm a point, I say so instead of guessing.


### Is Udio free to use in 2026?


Yes, Udio has offered a free tier that meters you in credits, and that's the unit to watch. I haven't confirmed the current daily or monthly allowance, so treat any figure you see quoted elsewhere as unverified until it matches Udio's pricing page.


Run your normal month on the free tier first. A counted month tells you whether you need to pay at all.


### Can I use Udio songs commercially on a paid plan?


Unconfirmed. Commercial rights are set by Udio's terms, not by the plan name, and those terms can differ between free and paid tiers and change over time.


Before you release or monetize a track, read the current terms and keep a dated copy. If you are paying mainly for commercial use, this is the line that decides whether the plan is worth it.


Does Udio offer refunds or a free trial? The free tier works as the trial, since you can generate before paying.


A refund policy is a separate matter, and I haven't confirmed one. Assume a charge is final unless the billing terms say otherwise, and read them before you pay for a year up front.


Do unused Udio credits carry over to next month? Unconfirmed. Whether leftover credits roll over or reset at renewal changes the real cost of a plan, because an unused allowance that disappears is money spent on nothing.


Check the account page for the balance just before and just after a renewal. That shows you what happens in practice.


### Is there an Udio API?


Unconfirmed. I couldn't verify an official public API, so I wouldn't build a workflow that depends on one.


Be especially wary of unofficial wrappers, which can break or breach the terms without warning. If automation matters to you, ask Udio directly before you commit to a plan.


Before paying, settle these in order:


- Count a month of generations on the free tier.
- Read the commercial-use terms as they stand today.
- Look at how credits behave at renewal.
- Confirm refund terms if you plan to pay annually.


Once those are settled, the plan choice follows from your own count instead of the monthly price.
